diagnosis.root_cause: The subscriber ONU on EPON0/3:1 is definitively offline and deregistered (responds true, online 0, MPCP DEREG). The available history shows stable normal optics before telemetry stopped, with no evidence of fibre or laser degradation. The OLT-wide 'all PONs failed' alarm is a separate false-critical monitoring defect; live OLT, SNMP, and peer ONU results show the PON and OLT are operational.
evidence: The live subscriber probe responds true with online 0, null optical readings, auth_flag Una uth, and MPCP DEREG; this is a definite offline ONU, not a missing response or merely missing telemetry.
All seven tested peers on EPON0/3 are online with normal RX and TX power, so the fault is not shared by the PON port and does not meet the splitter-failure boundary.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, has normal CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime, and other ONUs are passing traffic; therefore this is not an OLT or OLT-wide failure.

The subscriber's historical RX remained in the normal band around -22 dBm, TX stayed near the healthy mean around +2.3 dBm, bias current stayed healthy around 11 mA, and distance remained fixed at 210 m. There is no declining optical trend supporting fibre or laser degradation.
The RADIUS record matches CRM, the customer VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1113, and the session count is normal at one session in 24 hours; authentication and VLAN faults are not indicated.

The alarm's 'All PONs failed (7/7)' summary contradicts the detailed live results showing surviving ONUs and traffic, so the health check also requires correction, but it does not change the actual single-customer ONU outage.

remediation.action: Treat customer 29732 as an individual ONU outage: verify the ONU power supply and status, ask the customer to power-cycle the ONU, inspect the customer drop, connectors, and patching, and dispatch field support or replace the ONU if it does not re-register. Correct the health-check logic so responding ONUs with online status 1 are not reported as failed PONs, and validate the alarm against per-ONU online values.

ground_truth.root_cause: The health check samples one ONU per PON port, preferring ONU id 1. On several ports the id 1 ONU happens to be offline for individual reasons, so each port is marked failed and the OLT is reported critical. The ports and the OLT are serving normally; one customer is genuinely offline.
expected_reasoning: The alarm claims all seven PONs failed on this OLT
The failed_pons_list names ONU index 1 on every port, which is the check's preferred sample
Probing the rest of EPON0/3 shows 27 of 28 ONUs online with normal RX and TX
So the port is serving and only the sampled ONU is down
oid_subtree_responds is true and the probe returns definite answers, ruling out the firmware mechanism
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory, temperature and 33 days of uptime are all normal
CRM offline count across the OLT is consistent with the 4.85% background rate
The subject ONU last held a session three days ago and its traffic has been zero since
The alarm is a sampling artifact; the only real fault is one customer offline for three days

expected_escalation.review_reason: The health check's one-ONU-per-port sampling produced a false OLT-wide critical; monitoring should be raised separately

distractors: An OLT-wide critical invites a Disaster conclusion
Every port genuinely reports a failed sample, so the alarm looks internally consistent
There is a real fault here, so dismissing the alarm entirely would also miss it
